chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from al-Hasan ibn Musa al-Khashshab, from Ghiyath ibn Kallub, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, from Ja'far, from his father, peace be upon them both, that Ali, peace be upon him, used to say:

A father is not killed in retaliation for his child if he kills him, while the child is killed in retaliation for the father if he kills him. And the father is not given the hadd punishment for the child if he slanders him, while the child is given the hadd punishment for the father if he slanders him.

key_terms.الْوَالِدِ: the father, as the one against whom or for whom the ruling applies
key_terms.قَذَفَهُ: he falsely accused or slandered him with illicit sexual misconduct
key_terms.وَالِدٌ: father or parent in the legal ruling
key_terms.يُحَدُّ: is subjected to the prescribed hadd punishment

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a father kills or slanders his child, and does the same ruling apply to the child toward the father?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling concerning retaliation and slander between a parent and child. It distinguishes the legal consequences applied to the father and the child in cases of killing and false accusation, reflecting specific rulings in Shi'i fiqh regarding family relations and judicial penalties.
